hens_rule_text: Up to 10 fowl (chickens, turkeys, ducks, geese or guineas combined) allowed per residence in a securely fenced or coop area, no permit needed.
permit_notes: No permit required if the resident follows the city code's fowl-keeping rules in Sec. 4-31.
setback_notes: Coops must be kept at least 50 ft from a neighboring residence, unless the neighbor gives written consent to a shorter distance.
coop_rules: Fowl must be kept within a coop and a securely fenced area sized and located per the code's standards.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: City of St. Petersburg, Good Neighbor Guide: Gardening & Yard Animals (official PDF)
WFLA, Backyard chickens: Is it legal to keep chickens in Tampa & St. Pete?

research_notes: The city's own Good Neighbor Guide PDF (confirmed reachable, 200 OK, but text not extracted directly) is quoted in a search-result extract confirming 10 fowl, the 50 ft coop setback and the Sec. 4-31 citation; a rival secondary claim of a 4-hen cap was rejected as inconsistent with the official guide. No 2023 to 2026 amendment was found.
